_comment: Seeded 2026-07-28 from the live 3-seat reader-panel FAIL (review of the Franklin candidate): the ch01 quiz asserted an age for the Silence Dogood essays that contradicted the chapter's own narrative text. The sidecar's hardSpecifics are authoritative. RENAMED 2026-08-03 from autobiography-of-benjamin-franklin.json: the pipeline slugifies the title to 'the-autobiography-of-benjamin-franklin', so the old filename never loaded and every rule below sat unread for the entire canary. EXTENDED 2026-08-03 with the two content blockers left open in V25_CANARY_COMPLETION_REPORT.md section 6. Fact pins and safety rules moved from notes/phrases into prohibitions: those channels render under an OVER-USE header that grants a quota of one and tells the writer to paraphrase the item elsewhere, which for a banned variant means writing it once and rephrasing it everywhere else — the exact inverse of the intent. HONESTY NOTE: no Franklin research sidecar or panel-review JSON exists in this repo, so the virtue rule below could not be re-read from hardSpecifics. It is therefore written as a CONSISTENCY rule that defers to whatever count the sidecar states, not as an independent claim about the number.
prohibitions: FACT PIN (panel blocker): the Silence Dogood essays are written at 'age sixteen' — the sidecar's verbatim hardSpecific. Every surface (breakdown tiers, quiz prompts, quiz explanations, review cards, examples) must state the SAME age using that exact phrase. Never write 'not yet sixteen', 'before age sixteen', 'not yet age sixteen', or any other variant that contradicts it.

FACT PIN: the indenture was a nine-year contract, and roughly four years remained when Franklin left. Never write 'nine years still owed' or otherwise imply nine years remained at departure — say 'a nine-year contract', or name the remaining term correctly.

CROSS-SURFACE CONSISTENCY: a fact asserted in the breakdown and re-used in a quiz prompt, explanation, or review card must match word-for-word on the number, age, date, and direction of the claim. The quiz is not a place to re-derive or re-phrase a fact — quote the anchor's hardSpecific.

COUNT CONSISTENCY (panel blocker): the virtue list changes size within the book's own narrative — the moral-perfection program is drawn up at one count and a later friend's remark prompts humility to be added, giving a second count. That is why surfaces contradicted each other. Take the number from the chapter's research sidecar hardSpecifics and never re-derive it. Whenever a count appears, name the moment it belongs to ('the list he first drew up', 'after humility was added') rather than asserting a bare 'the N virtues'. Within one chapter the breakdown tiers, examples, quiz prompts, quiz explanations and review cards must all describe the SAME moment with the SAME number in the SAME words. Never write a quiz item whose correct answer depends on which paragraph the reader happened to read: if a prompt asks how many virtues, the prompt itself must name the moment.

SAFETY (panel blocker): never instruct the reader to begin unpermitted public works. Franklin's civic projects — street paving and cleaning, street lighting, the fire company, the subscription library — are HISTORICAL ACCOUNT of an eighteenth-century Philadelphia with no modern permitting regime. Narrate them in the past tense, about Franklin, as what he did. No action step, example, review card or quiz explanation may tell the reader to pave, dig, resurface, light, sign, or otherwise alter a street, sidewalk, or any shared or public property, and none may advise acting first and seeking permission afterward.

SAFETY: the transferable mechanism in Franklin's civic projects is the SUBSCRIPTION, not the construction — gather written commitments from the neighbours who benefit, then take the funded proposal to whoever actually owns the property (city, council, landlord, HOA, building management) BEFORE any work begins. Any example or action step modelled on one of these projects must show that permission-and-funding step ON THE PAGE. An example that opens with the work already underway teaches the unsafe version even when no sentence says 'skip the permit', because the reader copies the scene, not the caveat.
